quizzes.question: A frame draws three option cards, but its question has four options. What do you see?

options.label: The three cards answer; D in the band
Today's sheet, as before
The cards answer; D by its key only

quizzes.explain: A rule counts only when it finds one card for every option, so a frame with three cards for four options keeps today's sheet (A2).

quizzes.question: A video built before the band stops at a question. Where does the band go?

options.label: Over the frame's lowest eighth
Under the video, in room kept all along
Under the video, which shrinks while it is up

quizzes.explain: Its frames don't carry data-band="bottom", so the band goes under the video, in room kept for the whole video, and nothing resizes (A13, A14).

quizzes.question: You answered a quick check, and your pointer rests on the band. When does the video go on?

options.label: After ten seconds
After four seconds
Ten seconds after you leave the band, or on Continue

quizzes.explain: The count waits while the pointer or the keyboard is on the band, and starts again from the top when you leave; Continue goes at once (A18).

quizzes.question: You have sent your review, and now switch a call's verdict in the record. What happens?

options.label: It is saved, and goes with your next review
It is offered as Send the change
It is sent at once

quizzes.explain: After a send, any edit in the record is offered as Send the change, at the head of the record and in the Finish panel; nothing is sent until you press it (A10).

autonomy.chose: The frame's cards are answered through transparent buttons the player lays over them in its own page, placed from each card's box in the frame (percent of the stage), with the hover and focus ring drawn by the player
autonomy.insteadOf: listeners and a hover style injected into the frame's own document
autonomy.why: the frame's document is rebuilt by the runtime (a theme switch, a reload) and sits under the HyperFrames player's own click handling; the player's buttons are tabbable, keep the keyboard in the player, and need nothing from the frame but its boxes

autonomy.chose: Cards are matched by data-option, then by data-plan-option (the letter the system video, every walkthrough check and the bob-dylan check already carry), then by an id ending -opt-a / -option-a / -choice-a / -chip-a, and only then by the order of the elements whose class ends in -opt; a rule counts only when it finds exactly one card per option, each with a box
autonomy.insteadOf: data-option then the order of -opt elements only
autonomy.why: a survey of every question frame on the review page: order alone matched none of the quick checks in the walkthroughs or the system video, and a letter already written on the card is safer than counting; a frame where no rule finds every option keeps the sheet

autonomy.chose: A card on the frame shows its state as its button in the (hidden) sheet does: ticked or your answer ringed in ink, the right answer to an answered quick check in coral, with a small tag ("picked", "your answer", "the answer"); "recommended" is not tagged, the frame says it
autonomy.insteadOf: no state on the frame, only words in the strip
autonomy.why: the reviewer answered on the card, so the answer is marked there; reading the sheet's buttons (a MutationObserver) keeps both in step with one source

autonomy.chose: "Show the frame" is kept in the strip, and there it puts the question aside: the strip folds to one line ("Still to answer") and the cards and keys stop answering, so the frame can be marked; a mark tool that is on also takes the clicks from the cards (changed after review: under the video the band folds to that one line in its kept room; in the frame it folds to a pill in the corner of the empty eighth, m3)
autonomy.insteadOf: dropping "Show the frame" (the frame is no longer covered), or cards that answer while drawing
autonomy.why: the plan lists it; without it a reviewer who wants to draw on a question's frame would answer it by accident

autonomy.chose: A video leaves its lowest eighth for the band by data-band="bottom" on each frame's root (or once, on the video's own root); the band goes in the frame only when every frame that asks something carries it, decided once, when the runtime has mounted those frames (looked for up to about 8 s after ready); until then, and otherwise, it goes under the video
autonomy.insteadOf: a field in the storyboard's front matter lifted into the plan map, or a place decided per question
autonomy.why: the attribute is on what actually leaves the room, so a frame built without it cannot claim it; a video mixing places would still have to keep the room under it for its older frames, so it is one place per video

autonomy.chose: The band is an eighth of the video high, never under 72 px. Under the video its room (.bandroom) is kept for the whole video and the stage's height formula leaves exactly it (--band-k 8/9, --band-min 72 px), so the page still fits the window; what does not fit scrolls inside the band rather than growing it. On a phone it is in the page's flow, at least 104 px, and grows by a line when needed
autonomy.insteadOf: a band that grows with what it holds, or a fixed pixel height
autonomy.why: growing would move the transport under it, and a fixed height would be too small on a large screen or too large on a small one; on a phone the frame is the page's width, so a growing band still never resizes it

autonomy.chose: The band's layout: two lines. First the kicker, the question in its own words on one line in the serif (the whole question in its title) and Show the frame; then the hint and the acts, the act that goes on (Continue, Confirm) at the right in ink. Answered, the feedback (two lines at most) takes the question's place. Type scales with the video (cqw): the question 15–22 px, buttons 30–40 px
autonomy.insteadOf: the question in full, wrapping; or the strip's one line
autonomy.why: an eighth of the video holds two lines of reading-size type; the frame shows the question in full already, so the band's line says which question waits

autonomy.chose: In the frame, the captions are hidden while the band is up (not while it is folded), and come back when it goes
autonomy.insteadOf: leaving the captions
autonomy.why: the caption pill sits at y 880–1040, so the band (from y 945) would leave its top edge showing above it; while a question waits the band carries the words

autonomy.chose: A call always gets the strip, though its frame has no cards: Accept (A) and Flag (B) in it, and the call's "Instead of", "Why" and "Check" leave the player for the kicker's tooltip, since the call's frame shows them (changed after review: the strip is now the band; what the call chose is its one line of words there, in the serif, and its Accept and Flag are clear buttons)
autonomy.insteadOf: keeping the sheet for calls, or listing those facts in the strip
autonomy.why: the plan puts a call's Accept and Flag in the strip; every walkthrough frame for a call already draws what it chose, what it replaced and where to check

autonomy.chose: A group of calls in the strip: Accept all, then one "Flag A21" per call, named by its id as the frame names it; what each chose and replaced is in its button's title (changed after review: in the band, with "N more calls from this part." as its line of words)
autonomy.insteadOf: the sheet's list of the calls with a Flag on each row
autonomy.why: the grouped frame lists the calls; the list over it is what step 2 removes

autonomy.chose: On a touch screen the strip says "Tap a card." with no keys named, and its buttons drop their key caps (changed after review: the band's words; on a phone every key cap in the band goes, and its buttons are 44 px high)
autonomy.insteadOf: the desktop wording ("Click a card, or press A, B or C.")
autonomy.why: there are no keys to press on a phone

autonomy.chose: While the strip is up the stage gives it its height, so the page still fits the window: the frame shrinks by the strip (about 52 px at 1440×1000; more while an answered quick check shows its explanation, which takes a second line). On a phone the strip is simply in the page's flow (changed after review: removed; the owner saw the video shrink and grow back. The band's room is kept for the whole video instead, A14, and the video never changes size)
autonomy.insteadOf: keeping the frame's size and letting the page scroll under the strip
autonomy.why: the page's rule is the biggest frame that fits the window with its chrome; a strip pushing the timeline and Finish below the window breaks it

autonomy.chose: The 10 s wait is for a quick check answered just now; a question met again, already answered, keeps 4 s
autonomy.insteadOf: 10 s for every answered question met again
autonomy.why: the owner's words were about reading a quick check's explanation after answering; a rewatch past a run of answered questions would otherwise stop 10 s at each

autonomy.chose: "On the band" is the pointer over it, or the keyboard on any control in it but Continue; while held the count starts again from the top when let go, and the hint says "Waits while you are here". Only the band: the sheet (a frame with no cards) keeps counting under a resting pointer
autonomy.insteadOf: Continue counting too; or pausing and resuming the count where it was
autonomy.why: the player puts the keyboard on Continue after every answer, so counting it would mean it never goes on; a sheet is answered by clicking on it, so the pointer is always there

autonomy.chose: "Back to where this was explained": explained_at is a frame number or a composition id, lifted into the plan map as that frame's start (explainedAt, explainedFrame; one naming no frame warns and is left out). autonomy.insteadOf: a time in seconds in the storyboard; landing paused

autonomy.chose: The trip back is sent as a rewind (D-005)
autonomy.insteadOf: not counting it
autonomy.why: it is one, and the review's "rewound here" is the same signal: something there wanted saying more plainly

autonomy.chose: Reached again after "Back to where this was explained", a quick check waits with no count even when it was answered, as when opened from its mark
autonomy.insteadOf: the usual 4 s for an answered one
autonomy.why: the reviewer went back to look at it again; it should be there when they arrive

autonomy.chose: An open question the video leaves while playing (Play pressed with it up, or a seek away and then Play) gives way, and stops the video again when reached; a seek while paused still leaves it up, the frame moving under it; the rule that a question asked once and left open is never asked again is dropped

autonomy.chose: "change" opens a small editor under the answer: the question's options (a click saves; a pick-all ticks, then "Save the picks") and a line for own words (Enter saves); Esc closes it unchanged; no "Explain this more" there. autonomy.chose: An answer that was in own words, changed in the record, drops the comment those words made at the question; new own words make a new one

plan.title: Answer on the video itself, and edit the record in place
plan.problem:
When the video stops at a question, a sheet slides up over the frame and asks it again: the frame
already shows the question and its options as cards, and the sheet repeats both in a smaller, busier
form, covering part of what it asks about. You answer in the sheet, not on the thing you are looking
at. And the record is only partly editable: a comment's words can be edited there, and a comment or
a mark removed, but changing an answer ("change") sends you back into the video to be asked again,
and a call's verdict, a mark's words and a quick check's note can't be changed from the list at all.

steps.title: Click an option on the frame to answer
steps.text:
*Independent.*

While a question waits, the frame's option cards are clickable: hover and keyboard focus light the
card, a click answers exactly as the A–D keys do (a pick-all question ticks the card and waits for
Confirm). The same for a quick check's options. The player already reads each frame's page (it
marks the chosen option there after an answer), so this is the player's work, not the frames': new
frames mark each card with `data-option="a"`, and older frames, which don't, are matched by the
order of their option cards. A frame with no cards to match keeps today's sheet.

steps.title: A band, not a sheet: large enough to read, and the video never resizes
steps.text:
*Needs step 1 (the cards answer, so the band no longer repeats them).*

The question and its options are no longer repeated over the frame. What is left is what the frame
cannot do: answer in your own words, "Explain this more", a note on your answer, Confirm for a
pick-all question, "Show the frame" to look without answering, and a call's Accept and Flag (with A
and B as now). The first version put these in a thin strip under the video (question 1, answered
A), and your review found it too small to read, and that the video shrank to make room for it and
grew back after. So the band is redone: type at reading size, the question's own words in it, clear
buttons rather than links, laid out to match the frame's look; and its room is kept for the whole
video, so nothing changes size when a question opens or closes. Where it sits is question 2.

steps.title: Edit the record where it is listed
steps.text:
*Independent.*

In the record, the items that can't be changed there yet get their own small edit: a decision's
answer is changed in place, without going back into the video (the video routes as a fresh answer
would); a call's verdict switched; a mark's words edited; a quick check's note edited. Editing a
comment's words and removing a comment or a mark already work, and stay as they are. A quick check's first
answer stays as it is. After a review is sent, any edit is offered as "Send the change", as a new
comment already is.

steps.title: Check it on the videos already there
steps.text:
*Needs steps 1–3 and 5.*

Every video on the review page is played through its questions with clicks only, in light and dark
and at phone width: the plan videos, the walkthroughs and the system video. The record edits are
checked in the export the Finish panel sends; the video's size is measured before, during and after
each question and must not change.

steps.title: Questions keep pace with you
steps.text:
*Independent.*

Three things your review asked for:

- **A quick check waits longer.** After you answer, the video goes on by itself after 10 s, not 4 s,
  and never while the pointer or focus is on the band; Continue still goes at once.
- **"Back to where this was explained."** Every quick check has it: one click takes the video to the
  start of what the question tests (the first beat of its step, or a beat the storyboard names with
  `- explained_at:`), and the question waits there again when playback reaches it.
- **An unanswered question stops again.** A question you skipped past, folded away or never answered
  stops the video every time playback reaches it, until it is answered. (Answered ones come back
  answered and go on by themselves, as now.)

prerequisites.title: reelplanning: the whole system
prerequisites.gives: what the parts are and how a review goes

glossary.meaning: Turns plan.md into a video via HyperFrames
Voices the script, only the lines that changed since the last build; reelplanning build runs it, then finish-project and verify
The assembly tail: captions → index → plan-map → the terms index (which video explains each word) → plan-diff → the details check
Content-hash diff vs. the last committed build
<reelplanning-player>: where you watch, answer on the frame, mark, and press Finish
reelplanning review: serves the review page, takes the review when you press Send, keeps it in the inbox and hands it on once; sends the notifications
The agent's command from config.json, started by the review server when no session is waiting; auto mode, inside the sandbox, or without it (and the reviewer told) where this machine can't run it
scripts/reel.mjs; manages .reelplanning/; reel record logs a review's answers and files the review; reel status ends with memory
Acts on a plan review: approved, folds the comments into plan.md; changes requested, rewrites the steps a comment touched
Implements plan.md and logs each call the plan did not cover into walkthrough.md, with tags; its diff is then checked by a second, fresh agent (the code check)
Acts on a walkthrough review: changes the code for each flagged call; on changes requested, rebuilds only those beats
One video explaining the whole repo from spec.md; rebuilt where the spec changes
One pass by a reviewer, filed once as reviews/<kind>-<time>.json with a .md of what to act on; never overwritten. The player's download is annotations.json until it is filed

definedIn.title: Review loop, steps 3–4: record, then revise

glossary.meaning: The verdict at Finish. Approve (on a walkthrough, the build is accepted): the comments are acted on, no new video. Request changes: they are acted on, the touched beats rebuilt, and the video shown again

definedIn.title: Review loop, steps 1–2: finish, then send

glossary.meaning: .reelplanning/inbox/: reviews the review server has taken, each handed on once; not committed

The fence a headless run starts in: commands write only inside the repo, a hook keeps the file tools there too; checked before each run, and turned off, with the reviewer told, where it can't run (the hook stays)
A desktop notice from the review server: a video is ready, with what it will ask, or a headless run has ended

definedIn.title: Review loop, steps 5–6: rebuild, and you're told

glossary.meaning: A choice the agent made on its own while building, one the plan did not cover: one row in walkthrough.md. Labelled visible, hard-to-undo or close when you might want to overturn it

Which choices stop the walkthrough video: an off-plan change always, an unlabelled choice never, a labelled one until you have accepted that label ten times in a row, or again after a recent late fix with that label

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 3: the walkthrough video

glossary.meaning: What reviews show, worked out each time from the ledger and reviews/, never kept by hand: the lines reel status ends with, the evidence behind each in reel memory <id>; the reviewer's own, across repos, from ~/.reelplanning/you.jsonl (--you)
A late fix: something a review let through that a later plan, fix or review had to change. A recent one makes choices with its label stop the video again, however many were accepted in a row

A label the agent puts on a choice it made alone, saying why you might want to look at it. Four kinds: *visible* (you'll notice it when you use the thing), *hard-to-undo* (changing it later costs real work), *close* (a toss-up: the other way was nearly as good), *deviation* (an off-plan change). A labelled choice stops the walkthrough video; an unlabelled one does not

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 1: build, and log each call

glossary.meaning: How many times in a row you accepted choices with the same label. At ten accepted in a row, choices with that label no longer stop the video; one flag starts the count again from zero

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 3: the walkthrough video

glossary.meaning: An off-plan change: a choice where the agent did something other than what the plan said. It always stops the walkthrough video

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 1: build, and log each call

glossary.meaning: One scene of a video: a picture and a sentence or two of its voice. A video is a row of scenes; a question or a choice pauses at the end of its scene
A stretch of one video under one title; the player shows "Chapter 2 of 4" as it begins, and N / P jump between them. Not a plan's step, and not a part of the system
One part of the system, drawn as a box: the review player, the review server and the rest of this table's ids. system.json calls it a component; the system video says "part"
A plan of skill edits the memory's evidence supports, started by reel retro when reel status says one is due, and judged against a fixed benchmark
One scene per chapter for the choices that don't stop: each can be flagged, and Accept all takes the rest

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 3: the walkthrough video

glossary.meaning: One numbered part of a plan: one change, what it does and what it needs from another step (### Step N in plan.md); the video tells each in its own scenes. The system video tells its two loops in steps too
Where a review ends: you approve, or ask for changes, and send what you answered and marked

definedIn.title: Review loop, steps 1–2: finish, then send

glossary.meaning: decisions.md: every answer you gave and every choice you accepted, one entry each, numbered across the repo (D-056); an entry is never edited, only added to or marked superseded

definedIn.title: Review loop, steps 3–4: record, then revise

glossary.meaning: A question on what the plan or the code will do; "Expected something else?" sends your words to the agent as a comment

The answer bar. A question is answered on the frame's cards when it has them (own words, a note, Accept / Flag beside them); a frame with no cards gets the bar in the lowest eighth it leaves empty (data-band="bottom"), and only an older video without that gets it under the video; the video never changes size
Files a review of the system video and sorts each comment: fix the video, a small change, or a new plan

definedIn.title: Build loop, step 6: this video catches up

glossary.meaning: A page a beat opens beside the paused video, for what the video cannot hold; started from a template in templates/details/
Shows on a frame with a detail; click it or press O to open the detail
Where a detail opens: beside the stage on a wide window, covering it otherwise
The plan's own words from plan.md, one section per step, with the current step lit; off until the Plan switch (L) turns it on, then beside the video or in the record
check-details, run by finish-project and verify; a broken detail page stops the build
